jobs.title: Subcontract Program Management Mgr - L5
jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

This role will offer you the following daily challenges:
On the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) Program, Supply Chain is a key driver in providing buy component responsible for approximately 50% of the program hardware development subcontracts totaling three billion dollars of supplier value. The subcontractors we manage are vital in supporting design, build and deployment of the next step forward in national security detecting, tracking and destroying incoming intercontinental ballistic missiles in space before they reach American soil.

This Subcontract Program Management (SPM) Manager position on NGI will be a key member of the NGI Subcontracts Leadership Team and will have a team of subcontract administrators and subcontract managers as direct reports. In this role you will have the following daily key responsibilities:
- Support the NGI Subcontracts Organization in execution of the overall NGI program.
- Lead and manage a team of Subcontract Administrators (SCA) and Subcontract Managers (SCM) overseeing subcontractors or critical subcontracted systems for all contract types and programs, ensuring compliance with contractual requirements and company policies
- Monitor and support each Subcontract Management Team (SCMT) as they manage the overall cost, schedule and technical execution of their subcontractor. Each SCMT is expected to actively manage the supplier in delivering solutions on budget and schedule and develop and implement correction actions when necessary.
- Responsible for providing status reporting as required and support NGI program and Supply Chain business rhythm
- Ensuring compliance with all appropriate prime contract flow downs and being responsible for new business requirements, including RFP's to subs, technical evaluations, and Basis of Estimate requirements through negotiations and definitization of the subcontractor
- Overseeing the negotiation and coordination of additions, deletions, or modifications to subcontracts
- Engaging in Supply Chain strategy for the overall Strategic and Missile Defense mission area
- Attracting, developing, and retaining subcontract management talent to continually improve the group's performance
- Mentoring, coaching, and advising subordinates in their professional development
- Travel (up to 25%) to the program and subcontractor locations is required.

Basic Qualifications

To be effective, you will need to possess these basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree from an accredited college, or equivalent experience/combined education.
- 7+ years overall experience, with a minimum of 2 years of experience in a combination of subcontract and/or program management.
- 2+ years of overall experience in working with large subcontractors.

You will need to be a US Citizen and be able to obtain and maintain a US DoD SECRET clearance, to support this government contract, as well as successfully pass a drug and background check, in order to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. P lease note: No clearance is required to apply, nor prior to start.

Desired Skills

To be effective, ideally, you should also have:
- 3 years of current experience on large cost plus government programs
- 2 years of leadership experience
- Experience with Procured to Pay (P2P) and SC Nav or other SAP procurement platforms
- Experience with managing all contract types: Cost Plus, Incentive Fee, Firm Fixed Price
- Proven record of managing and delivering critical, large subcontract products, with focus on complex development subcontracts to deliver on time and within budget
- Ability to develop strong supplier relationships and positively supplier performance

jobs.title: F35 Training Operations Manager / Kleine Brogel / Belgium
jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

Lockheed Martin is seeking a Training Operations Manager (TOM) to support and lead F 35 training operations in Kleine Brogel, Belgium. The selected candidate will manage and execute daily F-35 training operations team activities, support Belgium Air Force (BAF) military pilots to maintain qualification levels using Full Mission Simulators (FMSims) and other F-35 Pilot Training Devices (PTDs), and assist to execute customer-approved pilot training syllabi, upgrades, and tactics training. The instructor will operate the Instructor Operating Station (IOS) and be an F-35 Subject Matter Expert (SME) supporting pilot training and tactics development, as well as recommendations for courseware updates.

The successful candidate will work closely with other members of the Lockheed Martin team at dedicated training sites to fulfill F-35 training and continuation training objectives. They will also implement and support Lockheed Martin initiatives, programs and policies, as directed. The candidate must maintain a Secret level security clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) access. They must also possess an appropriate degree from an accredited college, or equivalent experience/combined education, with professional experience and specialized training commensurate with assignment.

Primary duties include
• Build, coordinate and schedule daily training related activities and manage all permanent party and visiting RMS personnel.
• Manage personnel hiring actions, logistical coordination for base access and badging (IVRs), Visit Access Requests (VARs), SOU U/SOU C access, lodging, and site integration.
• Conduct daily, weekly and monthly coordination with the BAF to merge training priorities into a coherent, executable schedule to support customer needs and ensure contract obligations are fulfilled.
• Oversee continuous training (CT) and formal syllabi course preparation, including Scenario Generation development for all training missions, briefing guides updates, and that other instructional materials are converted to BAF standards.
• Coordinate with BAF Training and Standardization & Evaluation personnel to ensure proper training flow and execution of customer training programs, including syllabus adherence, instructor availability, and grade sheet completion.
• Manage and assist in the maintenance and advancement of the site’s training devices, including courseware and IT equipment arrival and integration, hardware and software installs, configuration management, audits and related activities, as directed by the RMS Enterprise team.

Additional Duties & Responsibilities
• Provide performance feedback and discuss career goals and development with employees.
• Assist in preparing training and maintenance schedules, maintain personnel training records, and ensure compliance with enterprise standards.
• Evaluate and track students from course start through graduation.
• closely with other Lockheed Martin team members at additional training sites to meet F‑35 schoolhouse and continuation‑training objectives.
• Support Lockheed Martin initiatives, programs, and policies as directed.
• Provide the designated customer representative a proposed “30‑90‑day” plan for PTD utilization, including scheduled maintenance downtime, for approval.
• Sortie Completion & Readiness Reporting (SCAR) – Submit accurate daily and weekly training and device information in a timely manner.
• Position may require rotating shifts, work in excess of 40 hours, and flexible coverage for on‑site customer requirements.
• Typically represented by an experienced pilot.
• Additional duties and related responsibilities will be assigned as needed.

Accompanied Status Available: New hires may have qualifying dependents accompany them on their long-term overseas assignment.
Foreign Location Premium(s): Available.

Basic Qualifications

• Candidate must have an active secret clearance with final adjudication within the last five years, and be able to qualify for, acquire, and hold a Special Access Program (SAP) clearance.
• Candidate should have flight time in fourth and/or fifth generation fighter aircraft.
• Must have in-depth knowledge of military publications and an understanding of fourth and/or fifth generation aircraft training operations.
• Candidate must have prior experience in delivering military pilot academics and simulator training, and be familiar with current instructional techniques and delivery methods.
• Proven ability to work collaboratively with cross functional teams and stakeholders from varied backgrounds.
• Outstanding interpersonal skills, excellent leadership traits, strong oral & written communication abilities, solid ability to organize, and a high desire to provide customer satisfaction.
• Demonstrated leadership skills and extensive professional experience in managing operations personnel supporting customer mission readiness at dedicated training and operational installations.
• Must be a proven leader with management style aligned to LM core values and Full Spectrum Leadership imperatives.
• Must have experience in evaluating personnel's performance and in completing performance appraisals.
• Use of Microsoft Office products (Word, PowerPoint and Excel) is required.
• Four year degree from an accredited college, or equivalent experience/combined education, with professional experience and specialized training commensurate with the assignment.
• Deployment and continued employment is contingent upon successful completion of the OJT required at Lockheed Martin’s training locations prior to the international assignment.

Desired Skills

• Experience interfacing with senior-ranking military customer representatives.
• Experience with F-35 pilot training curriculum.
• Familiarity with F-35 program requirements.
• F-35 system knowledge.
• F-35 Full Mission Simulator experience.
• Familiarity with the F-35 ALIS program.
• Currently possess F-35 Program special access.
• 1000+ hours Fighter Flight Time in fourth and/or fifth generation fighter aircraft.
• Previous experience as an F-35 Contractor Instructor Pilot (CIP) or F-35 Pilot Subject Matter (SME) experience.
• Previous experience with the Belgium Air Force customer.
• Familiarity with Belgium flight rules, procedures, and operations.

jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

WHAT WE'RE DOING
At Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, we’re building the most advanced and reliable rotorcraft in the world. Our mission is to deliver next-generation helicopters that meet the evolving demands of our customers — faster, more cost-effective, and with the highest quality possible. Within our Production Operations APEX (Achieving Performance Excellence) office, we’re leading the charge in driving transformational change across all our sites and product centers using Lean, Six Sigma, and business process management tools.

THE WORK
- As a Continuous Improvement Engineer in the Production Operations APEX office, you’ll be a key catalyst for change, partnering with teams across Operations to identify and implement impactful business improvements. Your role will include:
- Leading and supporting continuous improvement projects across all areas of Operations
- Applying Lean, Six Sigma, and Industrial Engineering techniques to reduce waste and enhance processes
- Serving as a business partner to Performance Management Teams (PMTs), guiding them in problem solving, conflict resolution, and alignment with key performance goals
- Performs activities involving the producibility and quality of the product, and the processes that directly pertain, encompassing primarily one or more of the following engineering disciplines: failure analysis, industrial, manufacturing, manufacturing equipment, process, product, quality assurance, reliability, supplier quality, Lean Six Sigma, test, and tool.
Defining project scopes, measuring ROI, facilitating cross-functional collaboration, and tracking key metrics
- Motivating and influencing cross-functional teams to drive a culture of excellence
- Supporting communication and change management strategies to ensure project success and long-term sustainability
- Participating in and sometimes leading special initiatives that require a strong foundation in project management and continuous improvement methodologies

WHO WE ARE
Sikorsky has been shaping the future of aviation for over a century. As the premier manufacturer of military and commercial rotorcraft, we’re proud to support those who serve and protect our communities every day. Backed by the strength of Lockheed Martin, we combine deep industry expertise with a forward-thinking mindset to push the boundaries of innovation in aerospace and defense.

WHO YOU ARE
You’re a passionate, results-driven professional with a talent for seeing the big picture and the small details. You’re energized by identifying inefficiencies and leading efforts to eliminate them — all while building strong partnerships and influencing change across an organization. You bring:
Experience with Lean, Six Sigma (preferably certified), and/or Industrial Engineering
Strong communication, facilitation, and team leadership skills
Proven project management experience with a track record of driving measurable results
The ability to motivate others, resolve conflict, and align stakeholders toward a shared vision
A continuous improvement mindset with a desire to make a tangible impact across the business

WHY JOIN US
At Sikorsky, you’ll be more than an engineer — you’ll be a change agent. You’ll have the unique opportunity to shape how we build the helicopters of tomorrow, improve the lives of those on the factory floor, and contribute to a culture of operational excellence that extends across the company. You’ll work alongside talented, mission-driven individuals who take pride in making a difference. Let’s elevate what’s possible — together.

Basic Qualifications

- 3+ years of related experience and may have a post-secondary degree or training in a related discipline.
- Lean Six Sigma Green Belt Certified
- Prior work in a production environment
- Demonstrates past experience in project management and leading teams
- Prior experience developing project business cases

Desired Skills

- Demonstrates ability to pull data from various sources, interpret, and develop actionable insights
- Past experience collaborating cross-functionally and working in a team environment
- Strong communication, presentation, and leadership skills
- Competent in using Microsoft Office suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, etc.)
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certified
- Previous knowledge of LM APEX and initiatives and/or Sikorsky Production System
- Experience working with a represented work force
- Understanding of Cost Account Manager (CAM) principles and Earned Value Management (EVM)
- Prior work experience in a continuous improvement role

jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

What is the mission?
The mission matters. So do the people behind it. With advancing defense technology at our core, what sets us apart is a culture of collaboration, purpose, and impact.
Space is a critical domain, connecting our technologies, our security and our humanity. While others view space as a destination, we see it as a realm of possibilities, where we can do more— we can innovate, invest, inspire and integrate our capabilities to transform the future.

What does this role look like?
Supply Chain’s vision is to enable customer and mission success through supply chain strategies and execution that deliver superior operational program performance and create competitive advantage through continuous improvement. It is our mission to deliver affordable supply chain solutions that meet all program requirements and manage supply chain risks to ensure positive supplier performance through all phases of the program life-cycle from capture to sustainment. If you are an enthusiastic, self-starter, eager to learn in a dynamic environment, come join our team. This is an ideal opportunity for you to make an impact on our supply chain strategy for robust, efficient, and fast program startup & execution.  Here, we are driven by innovation and integrity. By applying the highest standards of business ethics and a forward-thinking mindset, we believe everything is within our reach – and yours -- as a Lockheed Martin employee.

This role will offer you the following daily challenges:
Manages subordinate teams overseeing subcontractors or critical subcontracted systems for all contract types and programs, ensuring compliance with contractual requirements and company policies. Directs and manages all costs, quality, schedule, financial, and technical performance requirements that are levied on the subcontractor or the product family and is required to ensure performance and support of the contract milestones of the system. Responsible for and directs all phases of the subcontract from initiation of the business case for make or buy decisions through requests for proposals, transition to program startup, subcontract management plans, negotiation strategy, cost accountability, program execution, and contract closeout. - Bachelors degree from an accredited college in a related discipline, or equivalent experience/combined education,
- 8+ years of professional experience in either: Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Subcontract Administration, Subcontract Management, Negotiation, Proposal, Program Management, and/or Category Management.

- Ideal candidate will have at least 12 years of related professional Subcontract & Project management experience, as well as experience managing complex subcontracts, with a proven record of successful performance with focus on mission success.
- 8+ project management with experience working in the development phase of a program and with the ability to develop and execute to schedules.
- Proficient in Truth and Negotiations Act (TINA) and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR/DFAR) guidelines, and LMAP.
- Technical knowledge of space hardware products, and technical acumen with space programs and/or projects.
- Understanding of and experience negotiating and securing funding for complex long-term agreements.
- Demonstrated skills to drive culture change supporting enterprise initiatives (i.e. hardware commonization and insertion into programs, shift to "we vs. me" behaviors).
- Demonstrated effective use of metrics to drive execution and measure progress.
- Experience working in development phase of a program.
- Knowledge of manufacturing engineering processes.
- Proven ability to drive and inspire results/resolution of technical issues and successful outcomes through teamwork.
- Must have experience developing and delivering technical solutions with documented ROI.
- Proven ability to drive and inspire results/resolution of technical issues and successful outcomes through teamwork.
- Possess excellent communication skills, both written, verbal, and presentation, to effectively communicate business cases to all levels of peers, suppliers, as well as program and executive management.

- Proactively team with all levels of the organization and program customers.

jobs.title: Program Management Associate
jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

Directs all phases of programs from inception through completion. Responsible for coordinating subordinate employee recruitment, selection and training, performance assessment, work assignments, salary, and recognition/disciplinary actions. Responsible for the cost, schedule and technical performance of company programs or subsystems of major programs. Participates in the negotiation of contract and contract changes. Coordinates the preparation of proposals, business plans, proposal work statements and specifications, operating budgets and financial terms/conditions of contract. Acts as primary customer contact for program activities, leading program review sessions with customer to discuss cost, schedule, and technical performance. Establishes design concepts, criteria and engineering efforts for product research, development, integration and test. Develops new business or expands the product line with the customer. Establishes milestones and monitors adherence to master plans and schedules, identifies program problems and obtains solutions, such as allocation of resources or changing contractual specifications. Directs the work of employees assigned to the program from technical, manufacturing and administrative areas.

jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

The Senior Manager, Supply Chain AI and Digital Solutions will lead the identification, evaluation, development, and implementation of artificial intelligence and advanced analytics capabilities across the Global Supply Chain organization. This leader will serve as the primary bridge between corporate AI and technology teams and business-area supply chain professionals, translating operational challenges into practical, secure, scalable solutions.
The successful candidate will combine supply chain knowledge, technical acumen, and program leadership. This individual will partner with stakeholders across supply chain, programs, engineering, contracts, information technology, cybersecurity, legal, and other functions to identify high-value opportunities and guide solutions from initial concept through deployment, adoption, and benefit realization.
Initial areas of focus will include program and supplier performance, contract negotiations, and workforce efficiency . The role will assess where AI is appropriate, understand the capabilities and limitations of current systems and data, prioritize opportunities based on business value and implementation feasibility, and ensure solutions align with applicable security, compliance, data-governance, and responsible-AI requirements.

Desired Skills

- Develop and maintain a strategic roadmap for applying AI and advanced analytics across Global Supply Chain.
- Engage business-area supply chain leaders and practitioners to identify business problems, process inefficiencies, decision-support needs, and opportunities for automation or augmentation. Translate supply requirements into clear business use cases, functional requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation plans for AI and technology teams.
- Partner with corporate AI developers, data scientists, architects, IT teams, and system owners to evaluate the technical feasibility, scalability, integration requirements, and limitations of proposed solutions.
- Manage a portfolio of AI initiatives from discovery and proof of concept through pilot, production deployment, adoption, and sustainment.
- Establish measurable success criteria and track outcomes such as supplier performance improvement, schedule and cost performance, negotiation effectiveness, cycle-time reduction, productivity gains, risk reduction, and user adoption.
- Ensure solutions support established supply chain processes, policies, procedures, internal controls, contractual requirements, and regulatory obligations.
- Drive organizational readiness and adoption through change management, communications, training, workflow redesign, and user feedback.
- Maintain awareness of emerging AI capabilities and determine where commercially available, internally developed, or hybrid solutions best meet business needs. Promote reusable solutions, common standards, and lessons learned across business areas while accommodating legitimate differences in missions, systems, and operating environments.
- Develop clear business cases and recommendations for senior leadership, including expected benefits, dependencies, risks, investment requirements, and implementation options.

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, operations, business, engineering, computer science, data science, information systems, or a related field.
- Significant experience leading complex, cross-functional programs, projects, product implementations, or digital-transformation initiatives in a large, matrixed organization.
- Demonstrated knowledge of supply chain operations, with experience in areas such as procurement, subcontracts, supplier management, supplier performance, material planning, category management, contract negotiations, source selection, or supply chain risk management.

Standard Job Description

Role Overview
The Stock Plan Administrator leads the end‑to‑end management of Lockheed Martin’s global equity compensation programs, including PSU, RSU, and LTI Cash awards. This role collaborates with key internal stakeholders (HR, Legal, Finance, Payroll, Global Mobility) and external vendors to ensure accurate award processing, tax compliance, regulatory reporting, and employee education.
Key Duties
•    Execute the end-to-end administration of all global equity and long-term incentive (LTI) programs, including grant issuance, communication, retirement eligibility events, vesting events, and cash payouts
•    Calculate and process equity transactions with high accuracy, ensuring proper global tax withholding, trailing liability tracking for mobile employees, and timely reporting to local payrolls and Legal.
•    Prepare equity data for the Proxy, e.g., Grants of Plan Based Awards Table and Footnotes, Outstanding Equity Awards Table, Stock Vested Table, Payments Upon Termination Table and Footnotes, and PVP Table.
•    Enforce and maintain SOX controls, ensuring data integrity and compliance with internal equity policies.
•    Manage equity management platforms, perform cross-system data reconciliations, and generate reporting to support ASC 718 financial accounting and internal/external audits.
•    Serve as the primary subject matter expert for employee equity inquiries, designing and delivering clear educational materials regarding plan mechanics, vesting, and tax implications.
•    Partner strategically with HR, Legal, Accounting, Payroll, and Global Mobility to implement policy enhancements, execute mobile employee tax tracking, and streamline transaction workflows
•    Identify, design, and deploy process improvements and automation tools to increase operational efficiency, reduce scaling risks, and eliminate manual data entry.

Leads the development, implementation, and administration of compensation and incentive plan policies, procedures, practices, and programs. Responsible for subordinate employee recruitment, development, performance assessment, work assignments, compensation, recognition, and disciplinary actions. Provides guidance and makes recommendations to line managers and generalists on all compensation issues; and interprets local, state, and federal laws regulating compensation practices. May be responsible for executive compensation, HRIS functions, incentive plans and stock option administration. Communicates or oversees communication of compensation philosophy, plans, and incentives programs to all employees.

Basic Qualifications

Required Qualifications
•    5+ years of experience administering complex equity and incentive vehicles (RSUs, PSUs, LTI Cash, and Dividend Equivalents) within a large, publicly traded corporation.
•    Strong working knowledge of SEC rules, U.S. federal/state tax regulations, and internal SOX controls for equity compensation; experience managing international tax compliance and mobile employee tracking is highly preferred.
•    Proven proficiency with enterprise equity management platforms; specifically, Morgan Stanley at Work ShareWorks, SAP, and advanced Excel (XLOOKUP, PivotTables, data modeling).
•    Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with a proven track record of maintaining strict data confidentiality and detail accuracy.
•    Ability to thrive in a high volume, deadline driven corporate environment while managing multiple competing priorities with flawless execution.

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with a strong customer-service orientation to assist plan participants at all levels. Collaborative mindset with a proven ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships across HR, Legal, Finance, Payroll, and Global Mobility.

Desired Skills

Preferred Qualifications
•    Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related discipline.
•    Certified Equity Professional (CEP Level 3) designation or actively pursuing certification, strongly preferred.
•    Working knowledge of ASC 718 accounting principles and their impact on equity compensation and the corporation’s financial statements.
•    Experience with global mobility equity compliance and familiarity with other international securities regulations.
•    Experience using AI writing assistants to accelerate drafting, brainstorming, or summarizing tasks.
•    Experience participating in equity system implementation, data migration, or advanced reporting automation projects.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Eligibility:  Applicants  must  be Australian citizens and be eligible to obtain and maintain an active Australian Government Defence security clearance at the level required for the position.

SouthPAN is a Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) comprised of reference stations, telecommunications infrastructure, computing centres, signal generators, and satellites that provide improved positioning and navigation services in Australia, New Zealand, and its maritime region.

As a Cyber Systems Security Engineer , you will play a key role in delivering secure outcomes across complex Defence systems, translating cyber security requirements into practical engineering solutions and providing trusted technical advice to engineering, operational and program stakeholders. Drawing on your strong hands-on technical background, you will assess security risks, review system designs and influence security decisions throughout the system lifecycle.

This role is ideal for someone looking to build on their technical expertise and broaden their impact through technical leadership and advisory responsibilities. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, providing mentoring, knowledge transfer and guidance while taking ownership of security outcomes, coordinating activities across stakeholders and helping drive cyber security capability across the program.

This opportunity is based in Mawson Lakes, SA. Applicants from Melbourne, Victoria will be considered.

Key responsibilities

- Translate cyber security requirements into practical engineering solutions across the system lifecycle.
- Review system designs, architecture and technical changes to assess security impacts and ensure compliance.
- Conduct threat modelling, threat hunting and vulnerability assessments to identify and mitigate cyber risks.
- Support the development of cyber security requirements and the implementation, validation and verification of security controls and risk treatments.
- Provide technical cyber security expertise, troubleshooting support and guidance to engineering, architecture, operations and program stakeholders.
- Apply Defence and Australian Government cyber security frameworks, standards and policies to system architectures and solutions.
- Support security assurance, accreditation and authorisation activities, including risk management and reporting.
- Mentor and support technical teams while promoting cyber security awareness, best practice and continuous improvement.

What you’ll bring

- Significant experience in systems security engineering within Defence or complex ICT environments.
- Strong knowledge of Defence cyber security frameworks, including DCSAAF, ISM, PSPF, DSPF and SPARTA.
- Proven experience in security architecture, security requirements analysis, assurance, accreditation and risk management.
- Expertise in Linux administration, VMware environments, system hardening and platform sustainment.
- Experience with Elastic Security, SIEM technologies, security event monitoring and incident response.
- Strong understanding of network architecture, identity and access management, ASD-approved cryptographic requirements and secure system design.
- Demonstrated capability in vulnerability management, threat analysis and developing effective remediation strategies.
- Proficient in AI as it applies to this

Don't meet every requirement?

jobs.title: Senior Program Finance Analyst
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

Eligibility : Applicants must be Australian citizens and be eligible to obtain and maintain an active Australian Government Defence security clearance at the level required for the position.

As a Senior Program Finance Analyst, you will support program delivery by executing end-to-end project accounting for both R&D and customer-funded programs. You will deliver accurate internal and customer reporting, robust analysis and maintain effective control of program financial performance throughout the contract lifecycle, aligning with organisational financial rhythms and controls.

This role is ideally suited to a candidate with project accounting experience within Defence, engineering or government contracting sectors.

Key Responsibilities:

- Deliver timely and accurate financial reporting, including analysis of cost allocations, actuals, forecasts, and variances.
- Review program cost allocations and ensure compliance with established procedures.
- Support the preparation of budgets, forecasts, and associated assumptions through engagement with key stakeholders.
- Provide clear analysis, explanations, and recommended corrective actions for financial and reporting variances.
- Manage and reconcile OSEC reporting (Orders, Sales, EBIT and Cash), including booking orders and backlog reconciliation.
- Support customer invoicing preparation, debtor management, and cash flow tracking.

- Maintain accurate, audit-ready records and ensure compliance with financial controls, contract requirements, accounting standards, internal policies and procedures and Defence cost principles.

- Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting as required.
- Forecast and track ROS% performance, including the assessment and incorporation of adjustments.
- Review pricing proposals and estimates, ensuring appropriate financial assumptions and methodologies are applied.
- Apply an understanding of Defence Cost Principles and CASG Profit Principles.
- Liaise with relevant stakeholders on finance matters and contribute to the development of solutions for moderately complex issues

What you'll bring:

- Significant experience in program/project finance, management accounting, or commercial finance environments.
- CA or CPA qualified, or currently undertaking professional accounting studies.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify trends, patterns, and financial variances.
- Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and deliver accurate outcomes within agreed timeframes.
- Proven ability to adapt to changing business needs while maintaining a flexible and proactive approach.
- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate issues, identify root causes, and support effective corrective actions.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, with the ability to develop efficient and repeatable reporting tools to support Project Managers and the Finance team.

Don't meet every requirement?
If you're excited by this opportunity but don't meet every criterion, we'd still love to hear from you. Your skills and experience may be a great fit for this role, or another opportunity within our organisation.

Lockheed Martin is a dynamic organisation, providing stimulating and challenging opportunities with a global team of over 122,000 professionals. As a leader in national security, our innovative and diverse programs create a more secure future for Australia across space, air, land, sea, and cyber domains.

jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

You will be the Operations Analyst Manager for the Missiles and Fire Control (MFC) Industrial Engineering Center of Excellence in Orlando, FL. Our team owns the engineering foundation for how production work is defined, timed, scheduled and measured across the MFC manufacturing network, delivering consistent, high‑quality processes to machining, energetics, electronics integration, and test operations.
What You Will Be Doing
As the Operations Analyst Manager you will lead a multi‑site industrial‑engineering team, set priorities against inbound demand, and ensure the delivery of standards, capacity analyses, span‑reduction studies, and layout‑flow work. You will act as the champion for the engineering basis of work‑center efficiency, routings and scheduling parameters, and defend those standards to program, finance and operations leadership.
Your responsibilities will include
- Lead, staff, mentor and develop a team of industrial engineers supporting multiple manufacturing sites.
- Prioritize inbound work, deciding what the team takes on, returns with a defined method, or declines.
- Own delivery commitments for standards refresh, capacity and rate analysis, span‑reduction, and layout/flow projects.
- Maintain and defend the engineering basis for standards, routings, work‑center efficiency and scheduling parameters.
- Deploy common methods across sites so that capability resides in the process, not in individuals.
- Manage staffing plans, balance workloads, and charge effort against program and functional funding.
- Represent the function in governance forums, rate‑readiness reviews, and capital/footprint decision meetings.
- Hire, develop, and retain technical talent, handling performance management and succession planning.

Why Join Us
We are looking for a collaborative, results‑driven leader who thrives in a fast‑paced defense‑aerospace environment. You will shape the way MFC manufactures critical systems, work with cutting‑edge technologies, and influence a broad portfolio of programs. Lockheed Martin offers competitive compensation, a comprehensive benefits package, flexible work‑schedule options, and a culture that values innovation, growth‑mindset, and work‑life balance. If you are passionate about industrial engineering leadership and want to make a tangible impact on mission‑critical operations, we encourage you to apply.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or related technical discipline from an accredited institution
• 6 years of professional experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, operations analysis, or related field
• Demonstrated leadership of engineers or analysts as a formal supervisor or technical lead
• Experience owning delivery commitments across multiple concurrent efforts and competing internal customers
• Working knowledge of labor standards, routings, and ERP production data structures: work centers, lead time, capacity, order execution
• Experience presenting analysis and recommendations to senior operations, program, or finance leadership
• Experience working directly on a factory floor with production, planning, and quality
• Ability to obtain and maintain a US DoD Secret security clearance.
US citizenship required

Desired Skills

• Prior formal people leadership in an engineering or manufacturing function
• Experience leading a team supporting multiple sites or programs concurrently
• Direct SAP PP experience: routings, work centers, capacity planning, order execution, scheduling parameters

• Experience with capacity modeling, discrete event simulation, or factory layout at the network level

The Level 4 EVM/Supply Chain Coordinator ensures that the Control Account Manager (CAM) and Release‑Train Engineer (RTE) meet their daily earned‑value obligations while also serving as the central hub for professional‑services procurement and supply‑chain activities.  The role combines EVM oversight, supplier liaison, and full‑cycle procurement support to keep schedule, cost, and technical performance aligned with program objectives.

jobs.title: Operations Analyst Sr - E3
jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

Missiles and Fire Control is seeking an Operations Analyst Sr to support the Industrial Engineering Center of Excellence. This position sets and deploys the engineering basis for how production work is defined, timed, scheduled, and measured across the MFC manufacturing network. The selected candidate will:
• Develop and maintain engineered labor standards and routings, and defend the basis of those standards to program, finance, and operations leadership
• Analyze production spans, queue, and work in process to identify non value added time and quantify recoverable hours
• Build capacity and rate readiness models supporting production rate increase decisions
• Translate standards and work center efficiency into scheduling parameters that drive realistic system lead times
• Perform factory layout, flow, line balance, and takt analysis in support of throughput and footprint decisions
• Partner with site industrial engineering, production control, quality, and finance to deploy common methods across multiple locations
• Convert analysis into executive facing recommendations, stating assumptions and verification status of every figure
• Coach and develop site level industrial engineers on method, tooling, and analysis rigor
Work supports a range of MFC operations including machining, energetics, electronics integration, and test.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or related technical discipline from an accredited institution
- 5 years of professional experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, or operations analysis, or 3 years with a related Master's degree
- Experience developing and maintaining labor standards and manufacturing routings in a production environment
- Working knowledge of ERP production data structures: work centers, routings, operations, lead time, capacity, order execution
- Experience performing capacity, line balance, or throughput analysis on live production
- Demonstrated experience working directly on a factory floor with production, planning, and quality
- Advanced Excel and demonstrated ability to analyze large production data sets

Desired Skills

• Direct SAP PP experience: routings, work centers, capacity planning, order execution, scheduling parameters
• Familiarity with MIL-STD-1567A and the Type 1 and Type 2 engineered standard distinction
• Predetermined time system experience such as MOST or MODAPTS, and time study or work sampling experience
• Discrete event simulation experience such as FlexSim, Simio, ProModel, or AnyLogic
• Data tooling beyond Excel: Power BI, SQL, Python, or equivalent • MES experience, Apriso preferred
• Experience deploying a standard method across multiple sites, not a single plant
• Familiarity with EVMS concepts, earned value, and EAC development on a labor hour basis
• Lean, Six Sigma, or kaizen event facilitation experience • Prior experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated low rate high mix production

jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

The Employment Law Compliance Specialist will conduct investigations for both internal and external complaints relating to Lockheed Martin's compliance with federal, state, and local labor and employment laws and regulations, as well as support the company's defense of employment disputes. The Specialist may respond to agency charges and complaints, and assist with litigation and other actions for which the Employment Law Center of Excellence is responsible.
This role will not be responsible for overseeing litigation but will support the attorneys responsible for that function.
This position requires an understanding of equal employment opportunity laws, regulations, concepts, and practices.
The selected candidate must have experience conducting internal or external employment law investigations.
Experience supporting employers in administrative agency proceedings or in state and/or federal courts on employment law matters is desired for this role but not required, as is experience handling employment law matters from their inception as internal or external complaints through the agency process to resolution.
Responsibilities include conducting employment law compliance investigations, contributing to analyses to identify trends, and supporting efforts to potentially reduce complaints and mitigate risks.
The Specialist will also contribute to trend analyses and collaborate with internal stakeholders in legal, the Business Areas, and HR to determine appropriate corrective actions when needed.
Specific Responsibilities Include:
• Conduct impartial, thorough, and timely investigations of complaints involving race, ethnicity, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, US military veteran status, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, family structure, genetic information, or mental or physical disability, as well as compliance with other internal and external requirements. These will range from routine to moderately complex and include interviewing company personnel as a neutral fact finder, reviewing personnel documents, and analyzing employee data in a timely manner.
• Prepare written reports and summaries of findings, with supporting documentation, that are fair, impartial, and represent the facts
• Respond to agency charges, and support litigation when necessary
• Draft Position Statements for submission to external agencies for review by senior team members
• Provide information to and attend discipline review committee meetings to present investigation findings when necessary
• Liaise with Business Area leads and HR to convey findings resulting from investigations
• Support the centralized tracking of internal and external employment law-related investigations, complaints, inquiries, and charges across the enterprise
• Assist in responding to external inquiries and charges relating to employment law compliance
• Conduct research and analysis to contribute insight into legal trends as they relate to internal and external employment law-related concerns
•  Support training efforts relating to employment compliance topics
This position may require travel.
Close proximity to major Lockheed Martin facility preferred, may require onsite presence.

Basic Qualifications

•  Bachelor’s degree
• Knowledge of principles and practices of investigation and research, including interview techniques, principles and procedures of record keeping and reporting, research techniques, and data collection
• Familiarity with federal, state, and local laws, as well as court decisions and trends, regarding discrimination, harassment, and retaliation
• Critical thinking and the ability to analyze information in relation to internal policies, applying them to various situations
• Experience conducting internal or external employment law investigations.
• Experience preparing well-written investigative reports with supporting documentation
• Experience collecting, analyzing, and interpreting information received from investigations
• Exercises sound judgment, including the safeguarding confidential and sensitive information
• Performs detailed work with accuracy
• Must be able to travel as required

Desired Skills

• Exposure to employment law compliance work within a mid-to-large employer
• Experience supporting employers in administrative or legal proceedings relating to employment law
• Experience interacting with government agencies at the federal, state, or local level
• Ability to work collaboratively in a virtual team setting • Personal accountability, willingness to learn, and commitment to continual improvement
• Professional and clear communication style • Strong organizational and analytical skills
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities
• Familiarity with AI tools relating to legal analysis and responding to employment law-related concerns and inquiries
• Ability to work effectively across departments and functions
• Strong written and verbal communication skills
• Demonstrates integrity and sensitivity
• Familiarity with online case management systems supporting this function (i.e., COMET)
• Experience in Labor Relations preferred

The Operations Analyst will provide comprehensive program tracking, acquisition advisory, and strategic integration support to joint systems and specialized capabilities operating under Special Operations Command Pacific (SOCPAC). Located at Camp Smith, Hawaii, this contractor support position will assist the SOCPAC Cross-Functional Team (CFT) in navigating joint, multi-domain, and Special Operations Forces (SOF) requirements.
The primary focus of this role is supporting the logistical, financial, and contractual preparation required for SOCPAC's annual cycle of exercises. The contractor will assist in tracking the positioning of necessary contract vehicles, interagency agreements, equipment, and communications systems for joint exercises. This role focuses on advisory support for acquisition, budget tracking, logistics, and preparatory functions. The contractor serves as a liaison support bridge between SOCPAC SOJ-Directorates, joint service components (Army, Navy, and Marine Corps SOF), USSOCOM, service acquisition offices, and various System Program Offices (SPOs), acting strictly in an advisory capacity. Work will be performed on-site at Camp Smith, Hawaii, within a secure facility (SCIF) environment.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

Eligibility : Applicants must be Australian citizens and be eligible to obtain and maintain an active Australian Government Defence security clearance at the level required for the position.

The Finance Analyst (or Project Accountant) will serve as a key member of the RMS Finance Team supporting the AIR 6500 program. The role requires executing a range of financial functions including, budgeting/forecasting, cost accounting and reporting, to consolidate financial results (orders, sales, EBIT, cash, ROIC, overheads, discretionary funding) and deliver contractual cost and schedule reports. Leveraging multiple financial systems, the analyst performs variance, trend, and workforce‑planning analyses, identifies risks and opportunities. The incumbent develops forward looking dashboards and visual analytics that support strategic decision making and provides actionable financial recommendations to senior leadership and external stakeholders.

What you'll be doing:

- Generating month to month and period end reports that capture all key financial metrics (Orders, Sales, EBIT, Cash, OSEC, ROS%, and overhead costs), ensuring cost allocation accuracy and alignment with forecasted figures.
- Reviewing and reconciling program cost allocation actuals against established procedures, providing clear explanations and variance analyses to senior stakeholders.
- Assisting in budgeting and forecasting efforts by gathering assumptions, connecting with cross functional teams, and contributing to the consolidation of forecast data.
- Administering customer invoicing, debtor management, and cash flow monitoring to maintain healthy liquidity.
- Supporting contract audits, sample based true‑up processes, and ad‑hoc financial reviews (monthly, quarterly, annual).
- Tracking program profitability (ROS%) and developing insights that inform profitability and risk mitigation strategies.
- Collaborating with finance and program stakeholders to diagnose moderately complex finance issues and codesign effective solutions.

The role requires a strong analytical mindset, meticulous attention to detail, and the ability to translate financial data into actionable insights for a regulated, defence contracting environment

About You:

- Proven expertise in accounting and finance, with a strong handle on accounting principles, concepts, and standards
- A track record of delivering accurate financial analysis and insightful advice
- Experience liaising directly with customers or external stakeholders, translating technical financial information into clear, actionable communication
- Demonstrated ability to produce timely, concise written reports and presentations for internal and external audiences
- Advanced computer proficiency – competent in data analysis and report generation using MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and related financial tools
- Familiarity with enterprise ERP systems
- CA or CPA qualified (or undertaking studies)

Why you’ll fit in:
Your background aligns with the demanding, mission‑critical environment of the AIR 6500 Program, a perfect match for a finance analyst or project accountant who can turn complex data into strategic insight.

This is your chance to shape supplier offerings, devise creative new subcontracts, and negotiate and manage critical subcontractors to deliver disruptive new hardware that drive the success of a quickly growing business area with tremendous opportunity for advancement.

- Partner with Program Planning and Finance to ensure material plans, schedules, WBS structures, and contract requirements remain aligned.
- Resolve complex material and ERP issues , including costing, pegging, material master, and demand-related errors.
- Coordinate priority material movement through receiving, inspection, production orders, and other supply chain processes.
- Support contract closeout and excess material analysis to ensure effective management and disposition of remaining inventory.

- Strong analytical, planning, and problem-solving skills
- Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage competing priorities
- Ability to proactively identify risks and drive issues to resolution
- Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills

- Strong analytical, planning, and problem-solving skills

jobs.title: Cyber GRC
jobs.description:
About the role

Reporting to the EMEA Information Security Officer, the Information Security Engineer will be responsible for the security engineering, accreditation, and lifecycle assurance of classified and sensitive IT systems. The role will support the design, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of secure IT environments, ensuring compliance with UK Government, MoD, and Lockheed Martin security requirements.

The successful candidate will work closely with programme teams, architects, infrastructure engineers, accrediting authorities, and information assurance stakeholders to ensure security is embedded throughout the system lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities:
- Lead the implementation of Secure by Design principles across classified IT systems and projects.
- Provide security engineering expertise throughout the system development and operational lifecycle, ensuring security requirements are identified and implemented from concept through disposal.
- Conduct security architecture reviews, threat assessments, and technical risk analysis for classified environments.
- Support the development and maintenance of system security documentation, security architectures, and security operating procedures.
- Lead and coordinate system accreditation activities for classified and sensitive systems.
- Develop and maintain accreditation artefacts including Risk Management and Accreditation Documentation Sets (RMADS), Security Cases, Security Management Plans, and supporting evidence.
- Work with Accreditors, Security Controllers, and customer security representatives to obtain and maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) approvals.
- Ensure continued compliance with applicable regulatory, contractual, and customer security requirements throughout system operation.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate cybersecurity risks within classified IT environments.
- Conduct security assessments, vulnerability reviews, and compliance audits against corporate and government security standards.
- Support risk treatment planning and remediation activities.
- Ensure alignment with NCSC, MoD, JSP, NIST, and Lockheed Martin security policies and standards where applicable.
- Support incident response investigations affecting classified systems.
- Assist with vulnerability management, patch management, and security monitoring activities.
- Participate in security reviews and technical investigations to identify root causes and corrective actions.
- Provide technical guidance to system administrators and engineering teams on security controls and best practices.
- Collaborate with programme managers, solution architects, IT teams, information assurance practitioners, and customer representatives.
- Provide security guidance to project teams during system design, implementation, and operational support phases.
- Support customer and regulatory audits and inspections.

Required skills, qualifications and experience

- Strong understanding of Microsoft Windows Server, Linux operating systems, virtualisation technologies, and enterprise networking.
- Experience securing classified, air-gapped, or highly regulated IT environments.
- Knowledge of cloud security principles including AWS, IaaS, and PaaS technologies where applicable.
- Familiarity with security technologies including endpoint protection, SIEM, vulnerability management, encryption, and identity management solutions
- Demonstrable experience applying Secure by Design principles in complex IT systems and programmes.
- Experience conducting security architecture reviews, threat modelling, and risk assessments.
- Strong understanding of system hardening, security controls implementation, and security testing methodologies.
- Experience supporting system engineering and security requirements management within regulated environments.

Accreditation & ATO Experience
- Proven experience developing accreditation evidence and security assurance documentation.
- Experience obtaining and maintaining Authority to Operate (ATO) approvals for classified or regulated systems.
- Knowledge of UK Government and MoD accreditation processes and assurance frameworks.
- Experience working directly with accrediting authorities, security controllers, or customer assurance organisations.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to communicate technical security concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently while supporting multiple programmes and stakeholders.
- CISSP, CISM, or equivalent Information Assurance certification.
- Degree in Cyber Security, Information Security, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Experience within Defence, Aerospace, Government, or National Security sectors.

Additional Requirements
- Knowledge of UK Government Security Policy Framework (SPF), NCSC guidance, JSP 440, and Defence security requirements.
- Understanding of GDPR and UK Data Protection Act requirements where applicable.
- Ability to obtain and maintain UK Security Check (SC) clearance with willingness and eligibility to achieve Developed Vetting (DV) clearance.
- Occasional UK and EMEA travel may be required.

jobs.title: HR Operations Analyst Sr - E3
jobs.description:
Standard Job Description

Implements and administers human resources programs, policies, and practices. Responds to HR practitioner, leader, and other employee inquiries, questions and complaints; provides information, guidance and direction on HR programs, processes, and procedures. Tracks and compiles issue logs and complaints, researching and recommending solutions. Provides feedback on HR policy and programs to HRBPs, functional specialists, and leadership. This is not generally a client-facing position, and may be part of a centralized support team.
The Challenge
As New Employee Experience Lead, you will impact the experiance of thousands of new employees' careers from first year interns to Executives.  If you are passionate about showcasing our unique culture, mission, and values at Lockheed Matin to our newest team members, this may be the right opportunity for you!  What is the challenge?  Our On-Boarding function is in the midst of driving positive large-scale change and is seeking leadership to help us continue leading by example, developing and executing collaborative new hire stratagies while sharing the resources needed for all new employees to make a smooth and positive transition.
A Day in the Life
At the first impression of Lockheed Martin Aeronautics - Marietta, you will help shape the new employee experience beginning on day one.  From New Employee Orientation (NEO), Virtual New Employee Orientation (VNEO), Off-Boarding, Outplacement Services, Contingent Non-Employee Labor, applicable thrid-party purchase orders, audits, and more, you will have the autonomy to lead a variety of efforts within our On-Boarding Center.
Although your primary focus will be to ensure an effcient, positive, and seamless transition for our employees, may also find yourself:
- Participating in strategic initiatives that will continue to enhance the new employee experience and further streamline the on- and off-boarding process.
- Developing relationships with SME's across business functions to help ensure up-to-date and relevant content for our new hires.
- Gaining exposure to delivering a custom experience for Aeronautics Executives.
- Owning the execution of NEO orientation to ensure new hires, rehires, recalls, and transfers are supported and engaged about Lockheed Martin's mission, values, and culture.
- Partnering with internal organizations and thrid-party vendor/agencies regarding the provision of services.
- Facilitating employee and manager briefings for a cross-functional partnership for on- and off-boarding activities and services, ensuring an efficient and seamless transition for employees.

About You
In this role, your human resources experience coupled with your ability to positively lead and engage with those around you, will help you succeed.  Your ability to seek out answers to the unknown and the passion to persevere when encountering resistance is what sets you apart.  Analytical and a critical thinker, you can make a positive impact providing data-driven people solutions that are efficient, effective, and flexible.  Most likely, you are in your element presenting to a variety of audiences and communicate confidently when speaking to your work.

- Strong communication skills, both oral and written, and customer service orientation.
- Ability to work independently and execute projects with autonomy.

Standard Job Description

WHAT WE'RE DOING
The Command and Control , Battle Management, and Communications (C2BMC) system is a large, complex development, integration and test, sustainment, and fielding program for the Missile Defense Agency. The Program supports the Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS) operations and is fielded in 33 locations, including US Strategic, Northern, European, Pacific, and Central Commands. The system operates 24/7 over 17 time zones and is supported by more than 48,000 miles of Defense Information Systems Agency communication lines. The system is the integrating element for the BMDS linking regional, theater, and national commands into a single strategic command and control weapon system and provides a comprehensive view of the battlespace. C2BMC enables commanders at all levels to systematically plan, collectively see, and dynamically manage designated networked sensors and weapon systems to achieve global and regional mission objectives.
THE WORK
We’re looking for a Deputy Program Manager (DPM) to join our C2BMC program. In this role, you'll manage our operations, maintenance, and sustainment activities from the operational site of the MDIOC at Schriever Space Force Base in Colorado Springs, CO!
You’ll be the connective tissue between internal teams and external stakeholders, working hand-in-hand with Missile Defense Agency (MDA), the customer. The DPM will collaborate closely with the C2BMC team to drive priorities, manage day-to-day operations, and ensure flawless program execution. DPM role will include CAM responsibilities for control accounts in the sustainment and deployment area.
WHO WE ARE
Our engineers and program teams work at the forefront of next-generation technology. At RMS, innovation isn’t just encouraged—it’s expected. We pride ourselves on delivering mission-critical capabilities while fostering a collaborative, energized culture. We’re a team of problem-solvers, builders, and forward-thinkers committed to protecting what matters most.
WHO YOU ARE
You’re a strategic leader with a passion for program execution and a deep understanding of defense systems. You thrive in a fast-paced environment and are skilled at managing multiple priorities and stakeholders. You bring experience in program management, defense contracting, and cross-functional collaboration. Most importantly, you’re someone who takes ownership and gets things done.
WHY JOIN US
• Play a pivotal role in a program that supports U.S. and allied defense initiatives
• Work with cutting-edge tech and some of the brightest minds in the industry
• Be part of a mission that truly matters
• Grow your career in an environment that values innovation, integrity, and impact
